title: How can I automatically update Tuesday Sale UI at midnight without refreshing the page?
text: I’m working on a Shopify theme with a recurring Tuesday Sale that runs from Tuesday at 00:00 until Wednesday at 00:00 in the store’s time zone . The current implementation determines the sale status using Liquid: {%- assign sale_weekday = 'now' | date: '%w' -%} {%- if settings.tuesday_sale_enabled and sale_weekday == '2' -%} true {%- else -%} false {%- endif -%} This status controls the sale announcement and navigation menus. Product prices and “Save %” labels are rendered separately using variant prices and compare-at prices. The scenario A customer opens the website on Tuesday while the sale is active and leaves the tab open. When Wednesday begins at midnight, the page continues displaying the Tuesday Sale announcement and navigation because Liquid does not rerender automatically. The reverse also applies: a page opened on Monday does not automatically display the sale when Tuesday starts. 7 posts - 5 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant needs recurring sale UI to update at midnight without refresh.

title: [Feature request] Count orders as sales only when they're paid, in Analytics and for external tools
text: Hi everyone, If you accept deferred payment methods (Multibanco, bank transfer, cash on delivery, B2B payment terms), Shopify creates the order at checkout with “Payment pending” status and treats it as a sale straight away. The biggest impact is outside Shopify: external software, especially ad campaign management tools, reads every order as revenue, and purchase conversions are sent to the ad platforms before payment is confirmed. When an order is never paid, nothing corrects it. ROAS and MER are overstated, and campaigns optimise towards orders that never turn into money. Inside Shopify Analytics it’s the same: unpaid orders count as sales on the order date, and when they’re cancelled the reversal often lands in a different month. The existing workarounds don’t fix it: Each external tool would need its own logic to exclude unpaid orders, and most don’t offer it. Filtering by order_payment_status keeps the sale on the order date, so past months change when an order is paid later. The Payments report is cash-based but only shows gross amounts (with VAT and shipping), not net sales. What I’ve asked Shopify Support for: A store setting to count pending-payment orders as sales only when payment is received, across Analytics and in the purchase events sent to marketing channels and pixels (or an automatic retraction when an unpaid order is cancelled). An option in sales reports and ShopifyQL to report sales on the payment date instead of the order date. I’ve already submitted this through Shopify Support. If you have the same problem, please reply or like this post so Shopify can see how many merchants need it. Related thread: Net Sales Dashboard - Not Including Payment Due Later Sales Thanks! Jorge 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant needs deferred payment orders to count as sales only when paid.
